overall_comment: Strong capstone pair. B2.6 (division as equal sharing) is anchored in Dan's deal-one-to-each routine and made symbolic with the ÷ notation; B2.1 partner relationship is reinforced through fact-family triangles and the 4-fact reveal (3x4=12, 4x3=12, 12÷3=4, 12÷4=3). Expanded walkthrough names a real, grade-2-specific build-to-equation translation trap with three distinguishable wrong-answer forms (12=3x4, 12-3=9, 3÷12) and branches recovery accordingly, including the fact-family triangle as a structural anchor. Mae and Dan are explicitly OPTIONAL puppets with substitution paths (voicing, stuffed animals, anchor poster) which keeps the lesson runnable without specialty kit. Vocabulary is precise (dividend/divisor/quotient introduced verbally even though only 'division' and 'fact family' are listed in vocabulary_introduced) and the open Part 4 prompt ('how many DIFFERENT ways can they share 12 fairly?') invites strategy invention and factor discovery. Worksheet maps cleanly station-to-part with one deliberate transfer move (Part 2 T3 introduces 4-5-20, extending beyond the lesson's 12-only dividends). Single 3 is INSTRUCTIONAL_BALANCE: materials are everyday or paper-printable and time (12/25/13 = 50 min) is realistic for G2, but the lesson does not include an explicit no-paper, no-purchase voice/body alternative path of the kind Level 4 requires (e.g., a body-as-plate sharing routine using fingers as recipients). Consider adding to differentiation: 'No-materials version — children sit in a circle and use their hands as plates; teacher passes invisible cookies one at a time around the ring while the class chants the round number.' That single addition would push the pair to all 4s.
